title: Neovim’s Built-In Terminal Emulator
summary: This chapter covers Neovim's built-in terminal emulator across Tips 15-22, beginning with the distinction between Terminal mode and terminal buffers. It shows how to launch programs with :terminal, manage terminal buffers in windows, splits and tabs, and use Normal mode commands for scrollback, search, copying and gf. The later tips cover controlling a running process remotely with jobsend() and an ad-hoc :Restart command, customizing shell prompts inside terminal buffers, and avoiding nested Neovim instances with neovim-remote and $VISUAL.

concepts.name: Terminal mode
concepts.evidence: In Neovim, you get a new mode to play with: Terminal mode.

concepts.name: Terminal buffer corresponds to a process
concepts.evidence: A regular Vim buffer usually corresponds to a file on disk, whereas a terminal buffer corresponds to a process.

concepts.name: Terminal cursor versus Normal cursor
concepts.evidence: In a terminal buffer, you have not one but two cursors: the Terminal cursor, which is managed by the underlying program, and the Normal cursor, which is managed by Vim.
